purpose: Reconstruction of the CURRENT structural node identity/index mechanism, from production code, before any replacement design. Read-only analysis; no production code was modified to produce this artifact.

nodeKeyOrigin.evidence: types.ts:48 doc-comment calls nodeKey 'the stable identity the task asks for... never derived from fuzzy string matching' - true of matching exactness, false of uniqueness; nothing in stage-structure.ts or structural-index.ts ever checks whether a nodeKey has already been produced for a different physical occurrence.

discardedDisambiguatingField.note: Already computed per-occurrence at parse time (sibling order under the same parent) but never folded into nodeKey - the disambiguating information already exists and is discarded before identity is formed.

byKeyMap.collisionBehavior: last-charStart occurrence silently overwrites any earlier occurrence sharing the same nodeKey (ordinary JS Map.set semantics on a key that was never actually guaranteed unique)

childrenByParentKeyMap.collisionBehavior: every node whose parentSectionRef label matches a given key is pushed onto ONE shared list, regardless of which physical parent occurrence it actually structurally descends from

allNodesArray.note: allNodesSorted retains EVERY physical occurrence (nothing is lost from the flat list) - only the identity-keyed maps (byKey, childrenByParentKey) lose information. This is why the defect is describable as 'unreachable', not 'missing': the data exists but cannot be retrieved by identity.

mapsKeyedByNodeKeyOrLabel_repoWide.note: independent Map, built BEFORE structural-index.ts even runs, over the same collision-prone nodeKey
in-memory map feeding a DB upsert - collision propagates to a persisted row overwrite, not just a wrong read
highest-consequence discovery-layer finding: deliberately MERGES two discovered candidates sharing a colliding key
materiality contextual-floor inheritance (R11 forensic mechanism) keyed on this map

collisionCensusOnDsgrEvidence.note: This is real-world evidence the collision mechanism is not a theoretical/synthetic-only concern; it is preserved historical evidence, not re-derived or modified by this proposal.

childrenByParentKeyLevel2Recursion.evidence: scripts/architecture-proposal-node-identity-repro.ts Case B, synthetic-doc-b::6.06(a) collides a SECOND time one nesting level down, proving the defect recurses at every level, not only at the top SECTION level.

persistenceLayerIndependentCollision.missingDisambiguator: charStart (or any occurrence-distinguishing value) is not part of this formula
persistenceLayerIndependentCollision.collisionConsequence: the second physical occurrence's upsert `update` branch (persistence.ts:52) silently overwrites the first occurrence's persisted heading/ordinal/charStart/charEnd - a DB-level silent row overwrite, not merely an in-memory wrong-read
persistenceLayerIndependentCollision.authorsOwnStatedRationale: persistence.ts:19-27 doc-comment explicitly states this reuses the same nodeKey-format scheme deliberately ('one real identity scheme, not two') - the defect is a considered design choice that turned out to be wrong, not an oversight in that one function.

priorArtInSameRepo.note: A separate, earlier persistence layer (used by lib/contract-model/validators.ts, service.ts, stage-dependency-resolution.ts) already implements occurrence-safe parent/child ownership correctly: parentId is a real foreign key to another row's own server-generated id, never a label match. Confirms the general direction (occurrence-safe identity, not label-based) already works elsewhere in this codebase; Phase 2A's later in-memory structural-index.ts diverged from it.

twoDistinctFailureMechanismsProducingUnr.mechanismA_PARSE_COVERAGE_MISS: no regex family ever matches a real heading, so no node is created at all - a pattern-completeness gap, out of this ADR's scope (see ADR §12)
twoDistinctFailureMechanismsProducingUnr.mechanismB_OCCURRENCE_IDENTITY_COLLISION: a node IS parsed (possibly more than once under the same label) but the identity scheme cannot tell physically distinct occurrences apart - this ADR's subject
twoDistinctFailureMechanismsProducingUnr.note: Phase 3F.1.1's forensic taxonomy combined both under R17_STRUCTURAL_PARSER_EFFECT (58 of 89 residual cases); this proposal treats them as related but separately remediated.
